title: FortiGate Log Reference
description: FortiGate log types, subtypes, field schema, and the setting that turns each one on, compiled from the FortiOS 7.6.0 / 8.0.0 documentation.

confidence_key.verified: Field list and example log line pulled directly from Fortinet's published Log Reference.
confidence_key.typical: Schema follows FortiOS's standard log field conventions for that feature; log IDs confirmed, but not confirmed field-by-field against a specific build in this pass.

logging_prerequisites: Every subtype below also needs a log destination turned on: config log disk setting / config log memory setting (set status enable) for local logging, or config log fortianalyzer setting / config log syslogd setting (set status enable) to ship logs off-box. For traffic and utm subtypes, the relevant profile must be attached to a firewall policy whose logtraffic is set to 'all' or 'utm' (not 'disable') — a security-profile log toggle with logtraffic disabled never produces a log line.

common_fields.description: Calendar date and local time the log was recorded.
Event timestamp in epoch (nanosecond-scale) format — the authoritative sort key.
10-digit unique ID identifying the exact log message definition.
The two header fields this reference is keyed on.
Severity: emergency, alert, critical, error, warning, notification, information, debug.
Virtual domain (VDOM) the log was recorded in.
Serial number and hostname of the originating FortiGate.
Kernel session ID, used to correlate traffic and UTM logs for the same flow.
Source IP address and port of the traffic.
Ingress interface name and its role (lan/wan/dmz/undefined).
GeoIP country of the source address.
Resolved hostname and MAC address of the source device, when known.
Identified device type and OS, from device/user identification.
Destination IP address and port of the traffic.
Egress interface name and its role.
GeoIP country of the destination address.
Matched firewall (or security) policy ID and its UUID.
Policy category: policy, policy6, DoS-policy, interface-policy, etc.
Named service (from the service object) and IP protocol number.
Verdict for the event: allow/close, deny, blocked, pass, dropped, etc. (meaning is subtype-specific).
NAT disposition (snat/dnat/noop) and the translated IP/port.
Session duration in seconds (traffic logs).
Byte and packet counters for the session.
Identified application, its category, FortiGuard app ID, and risk rating.
Combined UTM verdict for the session and a cross-reference ID into the UTM log.
Free-text, human-readable summary of the event — present on nearly every log type.

traffic.description: Records traffic flow information, such as an HTTP/HTTPS request and its response, if any.

forward.note: The default policy-matched session log — the log you'll see the most of.

enable.cli:
config firewall policy
    edit <id>
        set logtraffic all
        set logtraffic-start enable
    next
end
enable.gui: Policy & Objects > Firewall Policy > edit the policy > Log Allowed Traffic > All Sessions (or Security Events for UTM-only).
enable.explanation: set logtraffic {all | utm | disable} on the policy: 'all' logs every session, 'utm' logs only sessions a security profile acted on, 'disable' logs neither. logtraffic-start enable additionally logs the session open, not just its close.

forward.example: date=2024-11-04 time=09:12:37 logid="0000000013" type="traffic" subtype="forward" level="notice" vd="vdom1" eventtime=1730714157 srcip=10.1.100.11 srcname="pc1" srcport=52134 srcintf="port12" srcintfrole="lan" dstip=172.16.200.55 dstport=443 dstintf="port11" dstintfrole="wan" poluuid="5a9c..." sessionid=8058 proto=6 action="close" policyid=1 policytype="policy" service="HTTPS" dstcountry="United-States" srccountry="Reserved" trandisp="snat" transip=172.16.200.1 transport=40772 appid=40568 app="HTTPS.BROWSER" appcat="Web.Client" apprisk="medium" duration=2 sentbyte=3521 rcvdbyte=15024 sentpkt=18 rcvdpkt=21 utmaction="allow"

fields.description: Resolved hostnames for source and destination, when known.
GeoIP country for each address.
NAT type applied and the translated source IP/port.
Application identification results for the session.
Session length in seconds.
Traffic volume counters.
Combined verdict across all UTM profiles applied to this session.
Endpoint identification fields from FortiOS device/user detection.
Cross-reference into related UTM log entries and app count for the session.
FortiClient EMS compliance tags matched by the endpoint, if any.

fields.field: hostname / httpmethod / referralurl / reqlength / reqtime / respfinishtime / resplength / resptime / resptype / scheme / statuscode / transid
fields.description: HTTP-transaction detail fields, populated when the forward session carries HTTP(S).

local.note: Traffic to/from the FortiGate itself. Same base schema as forward, dstintf="root" or a local interface, policyid=0 for implicit local-in traffic.

enable.cli:
config log setting
    set local-in-allow enable
    set local-in-deny-unicast enable
    set local-in-deny-broadcast enable
end

! FortiOS 7.6+, explicit local-in policies:
config firewall local-in-policy
    edit <id>
        set logtraffic-start enable
    next
end
config log setting
    set local-in-policy-log enable
end
enable.gui: Log & Report > Log Settings > Local Traffic Logging (or per local-in policy under Policy & Objects > Local-In Policy).
enable.explanation: local-in-allow / local-in-deny-unicast / local-in-deny-broadcast (config log setting) log implicit traffic to the FortiGate that isn't matched by an explicit local-in policy. On 7.6+, explicit local-in policies additionally need local-in-policy-log enabled.

multicast.note: Multicast forwarding (PIM/IGMP). Same base schema as forward, keyed by a multicast policy.

enable.cli:
config firewall multicast-policy
    edit <id>
        set logtraffic all
    next
end
enable.gui: Policy & Objects > Multicast Policy > edit the policy > Log Allowed Traffic.
enable.explanation: set logtraffic {all | utm | disable} on the multicast policy (older builds use enable/disable).

sniffer.note: One-arm sniffer / traffic mirror interfaces. Captured, not forwarded, traffic.

enable.cli:
config firewall sniffer-policy
    edit <id>
        set logtraffic all
    next
end
enable.gui: Policy & Objects > Sniffer Policy > edit the policy > Log Allowed Traffic.
enable.explanation: Same logtraffic {all | utm | disable} toggle as a regular firewall policy, set on the sniffer policy attached to the one-arm interface.

http-transaction.note: New in FortiOS 7.6 — per-HTTP-transaction detail inside a forward session.

enable.cli:
config firewall policy
    edit <id>
        set logtraffic all
        set log-http-transaction enable
    next
end
enable.gui: Policy & Objects > Firewall Policy > edit the policy > enable Log HTTP Transactions (under Logging Options).
enable.explanation: log-http-transaction enable on top of logtraffic all breaks each forward session's HTTP activity into its own transaction-level log line.

ztna.note: Zero Trust Network Access proxy sessions.

enable.cli:
config firewall policy
    edit <id>
        set ztna-ems-tag <tag>
        set logtraffic all
    next
end
enable.gui: Policy & Objects > Firewall Policy (ZTNA rule) > edit the rule > Log Allowed Traffic > All Sessions.
enable.explanation: ZTNA access rules are firewall policies matched on a ZTNA tag/certificate; logging is the same logtraffic setting as any other firewall policy — there's no separate ZTNA-only log toggle.

event.description: Records system and administrative events, such as downloading a backup copy of the configuration, or daemon activities.

system.note: Config, admin session, daemon, license events.

enable.cli:
config log eventfilter
    set event enable
    set system enable
end
enable.gui: Log & Report > Log Settings > Event Logging > System activity event.
enable.explanation: event enable is the master switch for all type=event logging; system enable turns on this specific subtype. Both live in the single global config log eventfilter block.

system.example: date=2024-11-04 time=08:02:11 logid="0100032002" type="event" subtype="system" level="information" vd="vdom1" eventtime=1730707331 logdesc="Admin login successful" sn="FGT60F..." user="admin" ui="https(172.16.200.10)" method="https" srcip=172.16.200.10 dstip=172.16.200.1 action="login" status="success" reason="none" msg="Administrator admin logged in successfully from https(172.16.200.10)"

fields.description: Human-readable description of the event (e.g. "Admin login successful", "Configuration change").
Serial number of the device that generated the event.
Administrator or daemon account associated with the event.
Access method and originating address, e.g. https(172.16.200.10), ssh(...), console.
Access method: https, ssh, telnet, console.
Source of the administrative connection and the FortiGate interface addressed.
What happened: login, logout, config-change, backup, restore, etc.
success or failed.
Failure reason when status=failed (e.g. invalid_credential).
Full human-readable message text.

user.note: Firewall authentication (FSSO, captive portal, 802.1X, VPN auth).

enable.cli:
config log eventfilter
    set event enable
    set user enable
end
enable.gui: Log & Report > Log Settings > Event Logging > User event.
enable.explanation: user enable under config log eventfilter (with the master event switch also on).

user.example: date=2024-11-04 time=09:05:02 logid="0102043008" type="event" subtype="user" level="notice" vd="vdom1" eventtime=1730710702 logdesc="Firewall authentication successful" srcip=10.1.100.11 dstip=172.16.200.55 policyid=1 interface="port12" user="jdoe" group="sales" authproto="FSSO" action="authentication" status="success" reason="none" msg="User jdoe authenticated successfully"

fields.description: Description of the authentication event.
Client IP and the resource/portal address involved.
Firewall policy that triggered the authentication requirement.
Ingress interface of the authenticating client.
Authenticated username and matched user group.
Authentication method: FSSO, RADIUS, LDAP, local, captive-portal, 802.1X.
authentication, logout, timeout.
Outcome and, on failure, the reason (bad password, account disabled, server timeout).
Full human-readable message text.

enable.cli:
config antivirus profile
    edit "g-default"
        set av-virus-log enable
        set av-block-log enable
        set extended-log enable
    next
end
! then on the firewall policy:
config firewall policy
    edit <id>
        set av-profile "g-default"
        set logtraffic utm
    next
end
enable.gui: Security Profiles > AntiVirus > edit the profile (logging is on by default) — attach it to a policy under Security Profiles > AntiVirus in that policy.
enable.explanation: av-virus-log / av-block-log enable logging on the AntiVirus profile itself (both default to enabled); the profile then has to be applied to a policy with logtraffic set to utm or all.

virus.example: logid="0211008192" type="utm" subtype="virus" eventtype="infected" level="warning" vd="vdom1" policyid=1 profile="g-default" srcip=10.1.100.11 dstip=172.16.200.55 url="http://172.16.200.55/virus/eicar.com" virus="EICAR_TEST_FILE" virusid=2172 dtype="Virus" filename="eicar.com" quarskip="File-was-not-quarantined." analyticscksum="275a02...1fd0f" analyticssubmit="false" ref="http://www.fortinet.com/ve?vn=EICAR_TEST_FILE" action="blocked" crscore=50 crlevel="critical"

fields.description: Detection category: infected, malware-list, oversize, analytics.
Antivirus profile that matched.
Resource location and file name carrying the threat.
Detected malware name and its FortiGuard signature ID.
Detection type classification, e.g. Virus, Riskware, Ransomware.
Reason quarantine was skipped, if applicable.
File checksum and whether it was submitted to FortiSandbox/Analytics.
FortiGuard reference URL for the signature.
blocked, monitored, quarantined.
FortiGuard risk score (0–100) and risk band (low…critical).

enable.cli:
config webfilter profile
    edit "g-default"
        set log-all-url enable
        config ftgd-wf
            config filters
                edit 1
                    set log enable
                next
            end
        end
    next
end
! then on the firewall policy:
config firewall policy
    edit <id>
        set webfilter-profile "g-default"
        set logtraffic utm
    next
end
enable.gui: Security Profiles > Web Filter > edit the profile > enable Log all URLs (or leave category log toggles at default-on) — attach it to a policy.
enable.explanation: The FortiGuard category filters log by default (log enable under ftgd-wf > filters); log-all-url enable additionally logs every URL request, not just the ones a category verdict blocked/warned on.

webfilter.example: logid="0317013312" type="utm" subtype="webfilter" eventtype="ftgd_blk" level="warning" vd="vdom1" policyid=1 srcip=10.1.100.11 hostname="ambrishsriv.wixsite.com" url="/bizsquads" method="domain" cat=26 catdesc="Malicious Websites" reqtype="direct" action="blocked" msg="URL belongs to a denied category in policy" crscore=60 crlevel="high"

fields.description: Filter mechanism that fired: ftgd_blk/ftgd_allow (FortiGuard category), urlfilter (local URL list), videofilter.
Requested domain and path.
How the category was resolved: domain, ip.
FortiGuard category ID and name.
direct request vs. referral.
blocked, passthrough, monitored, warning, authenticate.
Human-readable reason.
FortiGuard risk score and band for the category.

enable.cli:
config ips sensor
    edit "default"
        config entries
            edit 1
                set log enable
                set log-packet enable
                set log-attack-context enable
            next
        end
    next
end
! then on the firewall policy:
config firewall policy
    edit <id>
        set ips-sensor "default"
        set logtraffic utm
    next
end
enable.gui: Security Profiles > Intrusion Prevention > edit the sensor > filter entries (Log is on by default; enable Packet Logging if you want pcaps) — attach the sensor to a policy.
enable.explanation: log enable per filter/signature entry is on by default in the IPS sensor; log-packet enable additionally captures the triggering packet for pcap download.

ips.example: logid="0416016384" type="utm" subtype="ips" eventtype="signature" level="warning" vd="vdom1" srcip=10.1.100.11 dstip=172.16.200.55 hostname="example.com" attack="SQL.Injection" attackid=12345 severity="high" ref="http://www.fortinet.com/ve?vn=..." incidentserialno=695 msg="SQL Injection Attack" action="blocked" crscore=60 crlevel="critical"

fields.description: signature match, anomaly (rate-based), or botnet/malicious-url.
Signature name and its numeric ID.
Signature severity: info, low, medium, high, critical.
FortiGuard reference URL for the signature.
Sequential incident counter for correlation.
Action taken: blocked, dropped, reset, pass.
FortiGuard risk score and band.

enable.cli:
config application list
    edit "g-default"
        set unknown-application-log enable
        set other-application-log enable
        config entries
            edit 1
                set log enable
                set log-packet enable
            next
        end
    next
end
! then on the firewall policy:
config firewall policy
    edit <id>
        set application-list "g-default"
        set logtraffic utm
    next
end
enable.gui: Security Profiles > Application Control > edit the profile (Log Violation Traffic is on by default) — attach it to a policy.
enable.explanation: log enable per application-category entry (on by default); unknown-application-log / other-application-log separately control logging for traffic that couldn't be identified.

app-ctrl.example: logid="0228672" type="utm" subtype="app-ctrl" eventtype="signature" level="notice" vd="vdom1" srcip=10.1.100.11 srcmac="a2:e9:00:ec:40:01" srcname="pc1" hostname="fortiguard.com" app="HTTPS.BROWSER" appcat="Web.Client" appid=40568 apprisk="medium" incidentserialno=402 action="pass"

fields.description: signature (protocol/app match), im-* (IM specific), or detect-l2.
Application signature name and its FortiGuard ID.
Application category, e.g. Web.Client, Social.Media, P2P.
Application risk rating: elevated, medium, high, critical.
Client MAC address and hostname (from device identification).
Domain the application traffic addressed.
Correlation counter shared with IPS logs.
pass, block, reset.

enable.cli:
config spamfilter profile
    edit "default"
        set spam-log enable
        set spam-log-fortiguard-response enable
        config smtp
            set log enable
        end
    next
end
! then: set spamfilter-profile "default" and logtraffic utm on the firewall policy.
enable.gui: Security Profiles > Email Filter > edit the profile — attach it to a policy.
enable.explanation: spam-log enable is the main toggle; per-protocol log enable (smtp/imap/pop3/mapi and gmail/yahoo/msn webmail) controls which mail paths generate entries.

enable.cli:
config dlp profile
    edit "default"
        set dlp-log enable
        set extended-log enable
    next
end
! then: set dlp-profile "default" and logtraffic utm on the firewall policy.
enable.gui: Security Profiles > Data Loss Prevention > edit the profile — attach it to a policy.
enable.explanation: dlp-log enable turns on logging for the profile's matched rules; extended-log enable adds fuller detail per match.

enable.cli:
config firewall DoS-policy
    edit <id>
        config anomaly
            edit "tcp_syn_flood"
                set status enable
                set log enable
                set action block
            next
        end
    next
end
enable.gui: Policy & Objects > DoS Policy > edit the policy > enable Logging on each anomaly type.
enable.explanation: Each anomaly entry inside a DoS policy has its own log enable and quarantine-log enable toggle — logging is configured per detected anomaly type, not globally.

enable.cli:
config voip profile
    edit "default"
        config sip
            set log-call-summary enable
            set log-violations enable
        end
    next
end
! then: set voip-profile "default" and logtraffic utm on the firewall policy.
enable.gui: Security Profiles > VoIP > edit the profile — attach it to a policy.
enable.explanation: log-call-summary and log-violations are set separately under each of sip / sccp / msrp.

enable.cli:
config waf profile
    edit "default"
        set extended-log enable
        config signature
            config main-class
                edit 100000
                    set log enable
                    set action block
                next
            end
        end
    next
end
! then: set webfilter-profile / waf-profile "default" and logtraffic utm on the firewall policy.
enable.gui: Security Profiles > Web Application Firewall > edit the profile — enable Log on each signature class / constraint rule — attach it to a policy.
enable.explanation: Logging is set per rule (signature main-class/custom-signature, each constraint type, method, url-access, address-list) rather than with one profile-wide switch.

enable.cli:
config dnsfilter profile
    edit "default"
        set log-all-domain enable
        set sdns-domain-log enable
        set sdns-ftgd-err-log enable
    next
end
! then: set dnsfilter-profile "default" on the firewall policy.
enable.gui: Security Profiles > DNS Filter > edit the profile > enable Log all domains — attach it to a policy.
enable.explanation: FortiGuard category log enable (under ftgd-dns > filters) is on by default for matched categories; log-all-domain enable additionally logs every DNS query, not just filtered ones.

enable.cli:
config ssh-filter profile
    edit "default"
        set default-command-log enable
        set log shell exec sftp scp
    next
end
! then: set ssh-filter-profile "default" on the firewall policy.
enable.gui: Security Profiles > SSH Filter > edit the profile — attach it to a policy.
enable.explanation: log takes a list of SSH channel types to log (x11, shell, exec, port-forward, tun-forward, sftp, scp, unknown); default-command-log enable logs commands that don't match a defined shell-command rule.

enable.cli:
config firewall ssl-ssh-profile
    edit "default"
        set ssl-anomaly-log enable
        set ssl-exemption-log enable
        set ssl-handshake-log enable
        set ssl-negotiation-log enable
    next
end
! then: set ssl-ssh-profile "default" on the firewall policy.
enable.gui: Security Profiles > SSL/SSH Inspection > edit the profile — attach it to a policy.
enable.explanation: Four separate toggles cover the SSL event families: anomalies, exemptions, TLS handshakes, and negotiation events.

enable.cli:
config firewall gtp
    edit "default"
        set forwarded-log enable
        set denied-log enable
        set gtpu-forwarded-log enable
        set gtpu-denied-log enable
        set log-freq 1
    next
end
enable.gui: Security Profiles > GTP Profile (carrier-license builds) — attach it to a policy.
enable.explanation: forwarded-log / denied-log cover GTP-C, gtpu-forwarded-log / gtpu-denied-log cover GTP-U; log-freq throttles how often repeat messages are logged.

enable.cli:
config file-filter profile
    edit "default"
        set log enable
        set extended-log enable
    next
end
! then: set file-filter-profile "default" on the firewall policy.
enable.gui: Security Profiles > File Filter > edit the profile — attach it to a policy.
enable.explanation: log enable on the file-filter profile; extended-log enable adds more detail per match.

icap.note: ICAP offload to an external server, log IDs 60000–60002.

enable.cli:
config icap profile
    edit "default"
        set icap-block-log enable
    next
end
! then: set icap-profile "default" on the firewall policy.
enable.gui: Security Profiles > ICAP Profile — attach it to a policy.
enable.explanation: icap-block-log enable logs when the ICAP server reports an infection/block; the connection to the ICAP server itself is otherwise silent.

forti-switch.note: FortiSwitch security flow logging, log ID 56001.

enable.cli:
config switch-controller traffic-policy
    edit "default"
        ...
    next
end
! plus enabling flow/session logging on the managed FortiSwitch's security policy via FortiLink.
enable.gui: WiFi & Switch Controller > FortiSwitch security/traffic policy.
enable.explanation: Lower confidence than the rest of this reference — this flow log is emitted by managed FortiSwitches over FortiLink rather than a single documented FortiGate CLI toggle; verify against your specific FortiSwitch/FortiLink version.

enable.cli:
config virtual-patch profile
    edit "default"
        set log enable
    next
end
! then: set virtual-patch-profile "default" on the firewall policy (or local-in-policy for OT).
enable.gui: Security Profiles > Virtual Patching > edit the profile — attach it to a policy.
enable.explanation: log enable on the virtual-patch profile logs each detection; the profile is generally applied to local-in or OT-facing policies.

casb.note: Cloud Access Security Broker, log IDs 10000–10002.

enable.cli:
config casb profile
    edit "default"
        config saas-application
            edit "Microsoft_365"
                set log enable
            next
        end
    next
end
! then: set casb-profile "default" on the firewall policy.
enable.gui: Security Profiles > CASB > edit the profile > per SaaS application, enable Log — attach it to a policy.
enable.explanation: log enable is set per SaaS application entry inside the CASB profile, not once for the whole profile.

other_categories.note: Legacy top-level type (log IDs 18432–18434, DoS-sensor detections) — folded into utm subtype=anomaly on current FortiOS.
Log ID 65290 (LOG_ID_DEBUG_PRINT), internal diagnostic prints, not seen in normal operation.
